text:
jin: Quick async drop-in — short status: kernel + batching + KV cache perf. What I did: landed the microbatch shape change, added a guard to avoid empty-batch stalls. Ran small perf sweep on canary shard (p10/p95 looked fine). Blockers: one regression in long-context throughput when prefetch hits are ~<10%, need to tune eviction thresholds. Today: will wire up a metric for per-shard prefetch hit ratio and push a hotpatch for the eviction policy.

alex: thanks. saw the PR, left one small comment about atomics in batcher.cpp. think that could cause a rare race on shutdown.

jin: yep saw it, fixing now. quick question — should I prioritise conservative fix (mutex) or try optimistic refactor with CAS? conservative is safer and faster to ship.

maria: conservative mutex for now. ship safety then we can profile CAS in follow-up. :thumbsup:

sam: re: eviction thresholds — is the regression reproducible locally? I can try with the long-context harness.

jin: not reliably locally, only on canary under mixed workload. attaching small trace snippet: ```[shard=12] batch_start=160ms kv_prefetch_hit=0.08 tail_latency=42ms``` looks like cold tails + small batches.

ops-bot: Deploy Canary #4512 to cluster-runnable-3 finished — 3/3 healthy, 1 warning (kv-cache pressure spike)

alex: thanks ops-bot. jin — if it's kv pressure, maybe temporarily lower max_prefetch in config to reduce eviction churn. Could avoid the tail thrash.

jin: good call. I'll push a canary config change to set max_prefetch=64 -> 32 and add a perf probe. Will also include the mutex fix for batcher.cpp.

maria: ping me once canary is up, I can run the regression harness and confirm p95.

sam: if you want, I can hack a synthetic workload to stress prefetch hit ratio tonight.

jin: appreciated — will update with links. PRs: #8421 (batcher mutex hotpatch), #8422 (canary config bump). Expected deploy in ~30m. Blocker cleared if hotpatch stabilises.

alex: quick code-review ping on #8421 from me in a few minutes.

jin: thanks all :rocket:
